collector: apl-ax-collector pid=7157 (plain Pod outside the sandbox; reader Slack token, own S3 credentials, router GET /apl/result)

banner.text: PASS: all 3 required assertions passed with evidence (AX task (scripted driver))

limitations: Public challenge cases are visible to builders; they are not secret holdouts.
Hashes bind artifacts; they do not prove an honest collector.
Emulate's simulator routes accept any valid token; separation from the worker is proxy-enforced, not token-custody alone.
Ledger facts come from an export the in-sandbox coordinator wrote to the task's bucket; the collector reads it with its own credentials but cannot open the sandbox's ledger.

Slack transport limits (Emulate's documented gaps, docs/RESEARCH.md): Socket Mode, slash commands, shortcuts, exact rate limiting and interaction types other than button actions and modal submissions are not emulated; this lab exercises Events API callbacks and button actions only, so it makes no claim about those surfaces.
One collector identity per cluster: whether a second, separately allowlisted identity could read another tenant's results through the router is not tested.
One operator identity drives the AX API; a tenant is a namespace, an atespace and an Emulate workspace, not a separately authenticated AX tenant (L-034).
Both clusters are in one project and one VPC.
Isolation is judged only on traffic that leaves the sandbox through the egress gateway.

Isolation verdicts rest on a gateway-log extract the operator copies verbatim into the private set dir; the public MT-ISO export carries a copy with addresses replaced by roles, so the verdict cannot be re-derived from public files.
Cluster B's Substrate uses cluster A's snapshot transfer identity.
The ate-api-server Workload Identity principal is the same identity on both clusters, so its bindings on B's bucket also apply to A's ate-api-server.
One collector Secret holds every current tenant's fake credentials on its cluster.
